items.title: Check your engine oil
steps: Park on level ground and wait a few minutes after shutting off the engine.
Pull the dipstick, wipe it clean, reinsert fully, pull again.
Oil should sit between the MIN and MAX marks.
Top up a little at a time with the oil grade listed in your owner's manual.
items.note: Overfilling can be as harmful as running low — add small amounts and recheck.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Set tire pressure the right way
steps: Find the recommended pressure on the sticker inside the driver's door jamb (not the number on the tire sidewall — that's the maximum).
Check when tires are cold, before driving.
Use a gauge on each valve stem and add or release air to match.
Don't forget the spare if you have one.
items.note: Hot tires read higher, so cold readings are the accurate ones.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Jump-start a car safely
steps: Turn both cars off. Connect red (+) to the dead battery's positive terminal.
Connect the other red clamp to the good battery's positive terminal.
Connect black (–) to the good battery's negative terminal.
Connect the last black clamp to bare unpainted metal on the dead car, away from the battery.
Start the good car, wait a few minutes, then start the dead car. Remove clamps in reverse order.
items.note: Never let the clamps touch each other while connected.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Check tire tread depth
steps: Insert a coin into the tread groove (e.g. a US penny with Lincoln's head down).
If you can see the top of Lincoln's head, tread is about 2/32" or less — replace the tire.
Check several grooves across the tire; uneven wear can mean alignment or pressure problems.
items.note: Worn tread greatly increases stopping distance on wet roads.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Change a flat tire
steps: Get fully off the road, hazards on, parking brake set.
Loosen lug nuts slightly while the wheel is still on the ground.
Jack at the vehicle's marked lift point (see the manual) until the tire is off the ground.
Remove nuts, swap wheels, hand-tighten nuts in a star pattern.
Lower the car, then fully tighten in a star pattern. Recheck torque after a short drive.
items.note: Never put any part of your body under a car supported only by a jack.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Know your warning lights
steps: Red lights (oil pressure, temperature, brake) mean stop safely as soon as possible.
Amber/yellow lights (check engine, TPMS) mean get it checked soon.
A flashing check-engine light usually indicates a misfire — reduce driving and get it inspected.
Your owner's manual has the full list for your car.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Car audio basics: wire gauge
steps: Size power wire to the amplifier's current draw and the wire length — bigger amps need thicker (lower gauge number) wire.
Use the amp maker's recommended gauge as a minimum.
Fuse the power wire close to the battery (typically within about 18 inches).
Ground to bare metal on the chassis with a short ground wire of the same gauge.
items.note: The fuse protects the wire from catching fire, so it goes near the battery.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Car audio: set amp gain correctly
steps: Gain is not a volume knob — it matches the amp's input to the head unit's signal.
Start with gain all the way down and bass boost off.
Turn the head unit to about 3/4 volume and raise gain slowly until you hear distortion, then back off.
Set the low-pass filter for subs around 80 Hz as a starting point.
items.note: Too much gain causes clipping, which can damage speakers.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Check your coolant
steps: Only check when the engine is cool — never open a hot radiator cap.
Look at the coolant reservoir: level should be between the marks.
Top up with the coolant type specified in your manual.
Low coolant repeatedly can mean a leak; get it checked.
items.note: Hot coolant is under pressure and can cause serious burns.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Brake warning signs
steps: Squealing can be the pads' wear indicator.
Grinding means metal-on-metal — stop driving and get them checked.
A soft or sinking pedal can mean air or fluid leaks.
Pulling to one side when braking can indicate a stuck caliper or uneven pads.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Battery care
steps: Check terminals for white or green corrosion; clean with a baking soda and water mix and a brush.
Make sure the battery is clamped down tightly.
Short trips don't fully recharge a battery — take a longer drive occasionally.
Many shops will test your battery for free.
items.note: Wear eye protection; battery acid is corrosive.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Following distance
steps: Pick a fixed object ahead. When the car in front passes it, count seconds until you pass it.
Keep at least 3 seconds in good conditions.
Increase the gap in rain, at night, or when following large trucks.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Fix a running toilet
steps: Lift the tank lid and check the flapper — if it's warped or not sealing, replace it.
Check the chain: too tight keeps the flapper open; leave a little slack.
Adjust the float so water stops about 1 inch below the overflow tube.
Put a few drops of food coloring in the tank; color in the bowl after 15 minutes means a leaky flapper.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Patch a small drywall hole
steps: For small holes, apply spackle with a putty knife slightly overfilled.
Let it dry, then sand smooth.
For holes larger than a nail hole, use a self-adhesive mesh patch first.
Prime before painting so the patch doesn't show.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Unclog a sink without chemicals
steps: Remove and clean the pop-up stopper — hair is usually the culprit.
Use a plastic drain snake to pull out debris.
For kitchen sinks, try a plunger with the other drain sealed.
Clean the P-trap under the sink with a bucket underneath.
items.note: Chemical drain cleaners can damage pipes and are hazardous to skin and eyes.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Find the main water shutoff
steps: Locate your home's main shutoff before an emergency — often where the main line enters the house or near the water meter.
Check that the valve turns.
Also learn the small shutoff valves under sinks and behind toilets.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Reset a tripped breaker
steps: Unplug or turn off devices on the dead circuit.
At the panel, find the breaker that's in the middle or OFF position.
Push it fully to OFF, then back ON.
If it trips again immediately, there may be a fault — call an electrician.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Stop a squeaky door hinge
steps: Lift the hinge pin out (tap from below with a nail and hammer).
Wipe it clean and apply a light lubricant or a bit of petroleum jelly.
Reinsert the pin and swing the door a few times.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Caulk a tub or sink neatly
steps: Remove old caulk completely and clean the surface; let it dry.
Use painter's tape on both sides of the joint.
Cut the tube tip small and apply a steady bead.
Smooth with a wet finger or tool, then remove the tape before it sets.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Change your HVAC filter
steps: Find the filter size printed on the existing filter's frame.
Note the airflow arrow and point it toward the furnace/air handler.
Check it monthly and replace when it looks dirty, or per the manufacturer's schedule.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Test smoke and CO alarms
steps: Press the test button monthly.
Replace batteries per the manufacturer's guidance, or when it chirps.
Replace alarms at the end of their rated life (the date is on the back).
Have alarms on every level and near sleeping areas.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Hang something heavy on drywall
steps: Use a stud finder or knock to locate a stud and screw into it when possible.
If there's no stud, use anchors rated for the weight (toggle bolts for heavy items).
Check the weight rating on the packaging, and leave a margin.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Hold a knife safely
steps: Pinch the blade just in front of the handle with thumb and index finger.
Curl the fingertips of your other hand into a 'claw' and guide the food with your knuckles.
Keep knives sharp — dull knives slip more.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Dice an onion fast
steps: Halve through the root, peel, and keep the root end on.
Make horizontal and vertical cuts toward the root without cutting through it.
Slice across to get even dice. The root holds it together.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Cook fluffy rice
steps: Rinse rice until the water runs mostly clear to remove surface starch.
For many white rices, about 1 part rice to 1.25–1.5 parts water works; follow the package as a guide.
Bring to a boil, cover, cook on low until water is absorbed.
Rest covered off the heat for about 10 minutes, then fluff.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Safe cooking temperatures
steps: Use a food thermometer in the thickest part.
USDA guidance: poultry 165°F (74°C); ground beef 160°F (71°C); whole cuts of beef/pork 145°F (63°C) with a 3-minute rest; fish 145°F (63°C).
items.note: Color isn't a reliable sign of doneness — use a thermometer.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Season as you go
steps: Add salt in stages and taste along the way rather than all at the end.
A splash of acid (lemon, vinegar) can brighten a flat-tasting dish.
Under-seasoned is easy to fix; over-salted is hard to fix.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Get a good sear
steps: Pat meat dry — moisture prevents browning.
Preheat the pan until hot, then add oil.
Don't crowd the pan; cook in batches.
Leave it alone until it releases naturally.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Store leftovers safely
steps: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours of cooking (1 hour if it's very hot outside).
Use shallow containers so food cools quickly.
Eat refrigerated leftovers within 3–4 days.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Put out a grease fire
steps: Turn off the heat if you safely can.
Cover the pan with a metal lid or baking sheet.
Never use water — it makes burning oil splatter violently.
If it doesn't go out quickly, leave and call emergency services.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Boil pasta well
steps: Use plenty of water and salt it generously.
Stir in the first minute to stop sticking.
Taste a minute or two before the package time.
Save a cup of pasta water — its starch helps sauce cling.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Avoid cross-contamination
steps: Use separate cutting boards for raw meat and ready-to-eat foods.
Wash hands with soap after handling raw meat.
Don't put cooked food back on a plate that held raw meat.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Build a simple budget
steps: List your monthly take-home income.
List fixed costs (rent, bills) and variable costs (food, fun).
A common starting rule is 50/30/20: needs/wants/savings — adjust to your situation.
Track for a month and adjust categories to reality.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Start an emergency fund
steps: Open a separate savings account so it's not easy to spend.
Start small — even a small automatic transfer each payday builds the habit.
A common goal is 3–6 months of essential expenses.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Understand compound interest
steps: Interest earns interest on itself over time.
Starting earlier usually matters more than starting big.
The 'Rule of 72': divide 72 by the annual rate to roughly estimate years to double.
items.note: It works against you on debt too — credit card interest compounds.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Pay down debt strategically
steps: List debts with balances and interest rates.
Avalanche: pay extra on the highest-interest debt first (saves the most).
Snowball: pay off the smallest balance first (quick wins).
Always make at least the minimum payment on everything.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: What affects your credit score
steps: Paying on time is one of the biggest factors.
Keep credit card balances low relative to limits.
Long account history helps; avoid closing your oldest card unnecessarily.
Apply for new credit only when needed.
items.note: You can check your credit reports for free at the official site in your country (e.g. AnnualCreditReport.com in the US).
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Pay yourself first
steps: Set up automatic savings or investment transfers on payday.
Treat it like a bill you must pay.
Raise the amount when your income rises.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Avoid common scams
steps: Real banks and government agencies don't ask for passwords or codes by phone or text.
Be suspicious of urgency, gift-card payments, or crypto demands.
Call back using the number on your card or official website, not the one in the message.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Know your subscriptions
steps: Review bank statements for recurring charges each month.
Cancel what you don't use.
Set calendar reminders before free trials end.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Index funds in one line
steps: An index fund holds many stocks to track a market index, spreading risk.
They often have low fees.
Investing involves risk; values can go down as well as up.
items.note: This is general information, not personal financial advice.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: The 24-hour rule
steps: For non-essential purchases, wait 24 hours (or longer for big ones).
Ask: would I buy this at full price? Where will it live?
Impulse purchases often lose their appeal after a pause.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Squat with good form
steps: Feet about shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
Brace your core, push hips back and bend knees.
Keep your chest up and knees tracking over toes.
Go as deep as you can with a neutral back, then drive up through the whole foot.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Start moving without a gym
steps: Walk briskly — it counts as moderate exercise.
Bodyweight basics: squats, push-ups (incline if needed), lunges, planks.
Take the stairs and short movement breaks during the day.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Weekly activity guideline
steps: WHO adult guidance: at least 150–300 minutes of moderate aerobic activity, or 75–150 minutes vigorous, per week.
Plus muscle-strengthening activities on 2 or more days.
Something is better than nothing — start where you are.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Warm up properly
steps: Spend 5–10 minutes on light cardio and dynamic movements.
Do lighter sets of your first exercise before working sets.
Save long static stretches for after.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Progressive overload
steps: To get stronger, gradually increase weight, reps, or sets over time.
Log your workouts so you know what to beat.
Small, steady increases beat big jumps.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Hydration basics
steps: Drink water regularly through the day; thirst is a signal.
Pale yellow urine is a rough sign of good hydration.
Drink more in heat and during long exercise.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Sleep and recovery
steps: Most adults need 7 or more hours of sleep.
Muscles recover and adapt between workouts, not during them.
Keep a consistent sleep schedule.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Do a proper push-up
steps: Hands slightly wider than shoulders, body in a straight line.
Lower until chest is near the floor, elbows about 45° from the body.
Push back up without letting hips sag. Use an incline to make it easier.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Protect your back when lifting
steps: Get close to the object, feet shoulder-width.
Bend at hips and knees, keep the back neutral.
Lift with your legs and avoid twisting while carrying.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Listen to pain signals
steps: Muscle soreness a day or two after training is normal.
Sharp, sudden, or joint pain is a sign to stop.
See a health professional for pain that persists.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Hands-only CPR
steps: Check the scene is safe and the person is unresponsive and not breathing normally.
Call emergency services (or have someone call) and get an AED if available.
Push hard and fast in the center of the chest, about 100–120 per minute, about 2 inches (5 cm) deep for adults.
Keep going until help arrives or an AED is ready.
items.note: Take a certified CPR course — practice makes a big difference.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Use an AED
steps: Turn it on and follow the voice prompts.
Attach pads as shown on the pictures (bare, dry chest).
Make sure no one touches the person when it analyzes or shocks.
Resume CPR right after a shock or when prompted.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Help someone choking (adult)
steps: If they can cough forcefully, encourage coughing.
If they can't breathe, speak or cough: call for help.
Give back blows and abdominal thrusts as taught by your local first-aid guidance (e.g. Red Cross: 5 back blows, 5 abdominal thrusts).
If they become unresponsive, start CPR.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Treat a minor burn
steps: Cool the burn under cool (not ice-cold) running water for at least 20 minutes.
Remove jewelry or tight items nearby before swelling.
Cover loosely with cling film or a clean non-fluffy dressing.
Seek medical help for large, deep, facial, or electrical/chemical burns.
items.note: Don't use ice, butter, or creams on a fresh burn.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Stop heavy bleeding
steps: Call emergency services for severe bleeding.
Apply firm, direct pressure with a clean cloth or dressing.
Don't remove soaked dressings — add more on top.
If trained and bleeding is life-threatening on a limb, a tourniquet may be used.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: The recovery position
steps: For someone unresponsive but breathing normally.
Roll them onto their side, top leg bent to stop them rolling.
Tilt the head back slightly to keep the airway open.
Keep monitoring breathing until help arrives.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Recognize a stroke: FAST
steps: Face: is one side drooping?
Arms: can they raise both arms?
Speech: is it slurred or strange?
Time: call emergency services immediately and note when symptoms started.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Heat exhaustion vs heat stroke
steps: Heat exhaustion: heavy sweating, weakness, nausea — move somewhere cool, sip water, loosen clothes.
Heat stroke: confusion, very high temperature, possibly no sweating — call emergency services and cool them rapidly.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Build a basic first-aid kit
steps: Adhesive bandages, sterile gauze, tape, elastic bandage.
Antiseptic wipes, gloves, scissors, tweezers.
Any personal medications and an emergency contact list.
Check expiry dates periodically.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Fire safety at home
steps: Have working smoke alarms on every level.
Plan two ways out of each room and a meeting spot outside.
Get out, stay out, and call emergency services from outside.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Use a password manager
steps: Let it generate long, unique passwords for every account.
Protect it with one strong master passphrase.
Turn on two-factor authentication for the manager itself.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Turn on two-factor authentication
steps: Enable 2FA on email, banking and social accounts first — email resets everything else.
Prefer an authenticator app or passkey over SMS when available.
Save backup codes somewhere safe offline.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Back up with 3-2-1
steps: Keep 3 copies of important data.
On 2 different types of storage.
With 1 copy off-site (e.g. cloud or a drive kept elsewhere).
Test restoring a file occasionally.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Spot a phishing message
steps: Check the sender's actual address, not just the display name.
Hover over or long-press links to see where they really go.
Be wary of urgency, threats, or requests for codes.
When unsure, go to the site directly instead of clicking.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Speed up a slow computer
steps: Restart it — it clears memory and finishes updates.
Uninstall programs you don't use and disable unneeded startup apps.
Keep at least some free disk space.
Install system updates.
items.note: Avoid 'speed up' or 'cleaner' apps from unknown sources.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Keep devices updated
steps: Turn on automatic updates for your OS, browser and apps.
Updates often patch security holes that are actively exploited.
Replace devices that no longer receive security updates when you can.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Extend phone battery life
steps: Lower screen brightness or use auto-brightness.
Check battery settings to see which apps use the most.
Use the built-in battery optimization/charging features if your phone offers them.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Useful keyboard shortcuts
steps: Ctrl/Cmd + Z undo, + Shift + Z or Y redo.
Ctrl/Cmd + F find on page.
Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + T reopens the last closed browser tab.
Alt/Cmd + Tab switches apps.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Secure your home Wi-Fi
steps: Change the router's default admin password.
Use WPA2 or WPA3 encryption with a strong passphrase.
Update the router firmware.
Use a guest network for visitors and smart devices.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Take a screenshot
steps: Windows: Win + Shift + S.
Mac: Cmd + Shift + 4 (area) or 3 (full screen).
iPhone: Side button + Volume Up. Android: usually Power + Volume Down.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Write a strong resume bullet
steps: Start with an action verb.
Say what you did and the result.
Add numbers when you genuinely have them (time saved, customers served).
Tailor bullets to the job description.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Prepare for an interview
steps: Research the company and the role.
Prepare short stories using STAR: Situation, Task, Action, Result.
Prepare a few questions to ask them.
Practice out loud.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Negotiate a salary
steps: Research the market range for the role and location.
Let them make the first offer when possible.
Respond with a specific number backed by your research.
Consider the whole package: benefits, schedule, growth.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Give useful feedback
steps: Be specific about the behavior, not the person.
Explain the impact.
Suggest what to do differently.
Ask for their perspective.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Write clear emails
steps: Put the main point or request in the first lines.
Use a specific subject line.
Keep it short; use bullets for multiple items.
Say what you need and by when.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Run a better meeting
steps: Have a clear goal and agenda.
Invite only people who need to be there.
End with decisions, owners and deadlines.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Prioritize your day
steps: List tasks, then pick the 1–3 that matter most.
Do the most important work when your focus is best.
Batch small tasks like email.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Ask for a raise
steps: Document your results and added responsibilities.
Know the market rate.
Ask at a good time (e.g. reviews or after a win), and be specific.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Network without being awkward
steps: Be curious: ask people about their work.
Offer help before asking for it.
Follow up with a short thank-you note.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Handle a mistake at work
steps: Own it quickly.
Explain what happened and the impact.
Propose a fix and how you'll prevent it next time.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Pitch a tent
steps: Pick flat ground, clear of rocks, not in a low spot where water collects.
Lay the footprint, then the tent body.
Insert poles, clip the tent, stake corners at an angle.
Add the rainfly and tension the guylines.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Leave No Trace basics
steps: Plan ahead and prepare.
Travel and camp on durable surfaces.
Pack out all trash.
Leave what you find, minimize campfire impact, respect wildlife, be considerate of others.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Build a campfire safely
steps: Use an existing fire ring where allowed; check local fire restrictions.
Gather tinder, kindling and fuel wood.
Light tinder, add kindling gradually, then larger wood.
Drown, stir and feel — it must be cold to the touch before you leave.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Tie a bowline
steps: Make a small loop in the standing part.
Pass the end up through the loop, around the standing part, and back down the loop.
Tighten. It makes a fixed loop that won't slip and is easy to untie.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: The 'Ten Essentials'
steps: Navigation, headlamp, sun protection, first aid, knife.
Fire starter, emergency shelter, extra food, extra water, extra clothes.
Tell someone your route and return time.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: If you get lost: STOP
steps: Stop: stay calm.
Think: how did you get here?
Observe: landmarks, sun, trails.
Plan: if unsure, stay put and make yourself visible.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Avoid lightning outdoors
steps: When thunder roars, go indoors (or into a hard-topped vehicle).
Avoid peaks, open fields, and tall isolated trees.
Wait 30 minutes after the last thunder.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Treat water in the backcountry
steps: Boil, filter, or chemically treat water from streams and lakes.
Boiling: bring to a rolling boil for 1 minute (3 minutes at high altitude).
Prefilter cloudy water through a cloth.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Layer clothing
steps: Base layer wicks sweat (avoid cotton in the cold).
Mid layer insulates (fleece, down).
Outer layer blocks wind and rain.
Adjust layers to avoid sweating.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Bear & wildlife safety
steps: Store food properly (bear canister or hang where required).
Make noise on the trail.
Never feed wildlife; give them plenty of space.
Know local guidance for the species in your area.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Use a drill safely
steps: Wear eye protection.
Match the bit to the material (wood, metal, masonry).
Clamp small workpieces.
Start slow, then increase speed; let the drill do the work.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Find a stud
steps: Use a stud finder and mark both edges.
Studs are commonly spaced 16 or 24 inches apart center-to-center.
Confirm with a small nail in an inconspicuous spot.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Measure twice, cut once
steps: Hook the tape on the edge and read carefully.
Mark with a sharp pencil and a 'V' at the exact point.
Cut on the waste side of the line (the blade removes material).
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Pick the right screwdriver
steps: Match the tip type and size to the screw (Phillips, flat, Torx).
A wrong size strips the head.
Push in firmly while turning.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Use a level
steps: Place it on the surface and check the bubble is centered between the lines.
Check both directions for shelves and frames.
Longer levels are more accurate over long spans.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Tighten bolts the right way
steps: 'Righty-tighty, lefty-loosey' when facing the bolt head.
Use the correct size wrench or socket to avoid rounding.
Use a torque wrench where a spec is given (e.g. wheel lug nuts).
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Sand smarter
steps: Start with a coarser grit to remove material, then move to finer grits.
Sand with the wood grain.
Wipe dust off between grits.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Ladder safety
steps: Set it on firm, level ground.
For extension ladders, use the 4:1 rule: 1 foot out for every 4 feet up.
Keep three points of contact and don't stand on the top rungs.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Protect your ears and eyes
steps: Wear safety glasses for drilling, cutting, grinding.
Use hearing protection with loud power tools.
Use a dust mask or respirator for sanding.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Keep blades sharp
steps: Dull tools need more force and slip more easily.
Hone and sharpen chisels, knives and axes regularly.
Replace saw blades when they burn or bind.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: The 2-minute rule
steps: If a task takes under 2 minutes, do it now.
It stops small tasks piling up.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Calm down fast: slow breathing
steps: Breathe in slowly through your nose.
Breathe out longer than you breathed in.
Repeat for a minute or two. A long exhale can help you feel calmer.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Fold a fitted sheet
steps: Turn it inside out and tuck one corner into the next along the short side.
Repeat on the other side.
Bring the two doubled corners together and lay flat.
Fold into a rectangle.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Declutter with the one-in, one-out rule
steps: When something new comes in, something similar goes out.
Keeps closets and drawers from overflowing.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Make tasks easier to start
steps: Lay out what you need the night before (gym clothes, keys, bag).
Make the first step tiny.
Remove friction for good habits, add friction for bad ones.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Remember names
steps: Repeat the name back when you meet someone.
Use it once in conversation.
Link it to something memorable about them.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Reduce phone distraction
steps: Turn off non-essential notifications.
Move distracting apps off your home screen.
Use focus modes or grayscale during work.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Keep keys from getting lost
steps: Choose one spot by the door for keys and wallet.
Always put them there as soon as you come in.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Batch your errands
steps: Group errands by location.
Plan the route before leaving.
Saves time and fuel.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Quick room reset
steps: Set a 10-minute timer.
Put away items that are out of place, starting with the biggest.
Stop when the timer ends.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Active recall
steps: Close the book and try to recall what you just learned.
Write or say it from memory, then check.
Retrieving information strengthens memory more than rereading.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Spaced repetition
steps: Review material over increasing intervals (e.g. after 1 day, 3 days, a week).
Flashcard apps can schedule this for you.
Spacing beats cramming for long-term memory.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: The Feynman technique
steps: Pick a concept and explain it in simple words, as if to a beginner.
Notice where you get stuck.
Go back to the source to fill gaps, then simplify again.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Pomodoro focus
steps: Work for 25 minutes with no distractions.
Take a 5-minute break.
After 4 rounds, take a longer break. Adjust lengths to suit you.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Take better notes: Cornell method
steps: Split the page: a narrow cue column on the left, notes on the right, summary at the bottom.
Write questions in the cue column after class.
Cover the notes and answer the cues to review.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Interleave practice
steps: Mix different types of problems in one session instead of doing one type in a block.
It helps you learn to pick the right method.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Teach it to someone
steps: Explaining to someone else reveals gaps in your understanding.
Even explaining out loud to yourself helps.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Protect your sleep before exams
steps: Sleep helps consolidate memories.
An all-nighter often hurts performance more than it helps.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Practice tests
steps: Do past papers or self-made quizzes under timed conditions.
Review every mistake and why you made it.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Study environment
steps: Pick a consistent, quiet place.
Phone in another room or on focus mode.
Have everything you need before you start.
items.sourceName: Lumen tip card (written summary of common guidance)

items.title: Why the Moon has phases
steps: The Moon doesn't make light; it reflects sunlight.
Half of it is always lit, but as it orbits Earth (~29.5 days per cycle) we see different amounts of that lit half.
New moon: lit side faces away. Full moon: lit side faces us.
items.note: Phases are not caused by Earth's shadow — that's a lunar eclipse.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Why we have seasons
steps: Earth's axis is tilted about 23.5°.
For part of the year your hemisphere leans toward the Sun: sunlight hits more directly and days are longer → summer.
Leaning away gives low-angle light and short days → winter.
items.note: It's not about distance: Earth is actually closest to the Sun in early January.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: How far is a light-year?
steps: A light-year is a distance, not a time: how far light travels in one year.
That's about 9.46 trillion km (5.88 trillion miles).
The nearest star after the Sun, Proxima Centauri, is about 4.2 light-years away.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: What is a black hole?
steps: A region where gravity is so strong nothing, not even light, can escape.
The boundary is the event horizon.
Stellar black holes form when very massive stars collapse; supermassive ones sit at galaxy centers.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Read the night sky
steps: Planets usually shine steadily while stars twinkle.
Planets stay near the ecliptic, the Sun's path across the sky.
Free apps like Stellarium identify what you're looking at.
items.note: Let your eyes adapt to darkness for ~20 minutes and use red light.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Why is the sky blue?
steps: Sunlight contains all colors.
Air molecules scatter short (blue) wavelengths much more than long (red) ones — Rayleigh scattering.
At sunset light crosses more air, so blue is scattered away and reds/oranges remain.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Newton's three laws in one minute
steps: 1) Objects keep doing what they're doing unless a force acts on them (inertia).
2) Force = mass × acceleration (F = ma).
3) Every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Energy is conserved
steps: Energy can change form (motion, heat, chemical, electrical) but the total stays the same in a closed system.
'Losing' energy usually means it turned into heat.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Why a seatbelt works
steps: Stopping takes force; force = change in momentum ÷ time.
Seatbelts and airbags stretch the stopping time, which lowers the force on your body.
items.note: Same reason you bend your knees when landing a jump.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Volts, amps and watts
steps: Voltage is electrical 'pressure', current (amps) is flow, resistance resists flow.
Ohm's law: V = I × R.
Power (watts) = volts × amps.
items.note: This is why higher-wattage amps need thicker wire: more current.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Why things float
steps: An object is pushed up by a force equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces (Archimedes).
If it displaces its own weight before fully submerging, it floats.
Steel ships float because their shape displaces a lot of water.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Speed of sound vs light
steps: Light travels about 300,000 km/s; sound in air about 343 m/s.
Count seconds between lightning and thunder: divide by 3 for km (or by 5 for miles).
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Percent change, fast
steps: Percent change = (new − old) ÷ old × 100.
A 50% drop needs a 100% gain to recover.
Swap trick: 8% of 25 = 25% of 8 = 2.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: The rule of 72
steps: Divide 72 by an annual growth rate to estimate years to double.
At 6% a year, money doubles in about 12 years.
Works for inflation too: at 3%, prices double in ~24 years.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Estimate tips in your head
steps: 10%: move the decimal one place left.
20%: double that.
15%: 10% plus half of it.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Probability isn't 'due'
steps: Independent events like coin flips have no memory.
After five heads, the next flip is still 50/50.
Believing otherwise is the gambler's fallacy.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Mean vs median
steps: The mean is the average; the median is the middle value.
A few extreme values pull the mean but barely move the median.
That's why 'median income' is often more representative.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Area and volume scale fast
steps: Double a shape's length: area grows 4× and volume 8×.
An 8" sub has about 1.8× the cone area of a 6" one (ratio of diameters squared, not 1.33×).
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Why you never mix bleach and ammonia
steps: Bleach + ammonia releases toxic chloramine gases.
Bleach + acids (some toilet and descaling cleaners) releases chlorine gas.
Use one product, rinse, and ventilate.
items.note: If exposed, get to fresh air and contact poison control or emergency services.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: pH in one card
steps: pH runs 0–14: below 7 is acidic, 7 is neutral, above 7 is basic.
Each step is 10×: pH 3 is ten times more acidic than pH 4.
Lemon juice ~2, pure water 7, baking soda solution ~8–9.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Why rust happens
steps: Iron + oxygen + water → iron oxide (rust).
Salt speeds it up by helping electrons move, which is why winter road salt eats cars.
Paint, oil, or zinc coatings (galvanizing) block it.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Why salt melts ice
steps: Dissolved salt lowers the freezing point of water.
Ice touching salty water melts even below 0 °C.
It works poorly below about −10 °C (14 °F).
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Baking soda vs baking powder
steps: Baking soda is a base; it needs an acid (buttermilk, yogurt, lemon) to release CO₂.
Baking powder contains its own acid.
Both make bubbles that lift the dough.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Why antibiotics don't work on colds
steps: Colds and flu are caused by viruses.
Antibiotics kill or block bacteria, not viruses.
Taking them unnecessarily helps breed resistant bacteria.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: What DNA actually does
steps: DNA is a code made of four bases: A, T, C, G.
Genes are stretches that tell cells how to build proteins.
Almost every cell in your body carries the same DNA; cells differ by which genes are switched on.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: How vaccines train immunity
steps: A vaccine shows your immune system a harmless piece or version of a germ.
Your body makes antibodies and memory cells.
If you meet the real germ later, the response is faster and stronger.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Why sleep matters
steps: During sleep the brain consolidates memories.
Chronic short sleep is linked to worse focus, mood, and immune function.
Most adults need about 7–9 hours.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Your gut microbiome
steps: Trillions of microbes live in your gut and help digest fiber.
A varied, fiber-rich diet supports a more diverse microbiome.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Weather vs climate
steps: Weather is what happens today; climate is the long-term average (usually 30+ years).
One cold day doesn't change the climate trend, just like one hot day doesn't prove it.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Why earthquakes happen
steps: Earth's crust is broken into tectonic plates that move a few cm a year.
Stress builds where plates lock, then releases suddenly.
Each whole step up the magnitude scale is about 32× more energy.
items.note: During shaking: Drop, Cover, Hold On.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: The greenhouse effect
steps: Sunlight warms the surface; the surface gives off infrared heat.
Gases like CO₂ and water vapor absorb some of that heat and re-emit it, warming the lower atmosphere.
More CO₂ strengthens this effect.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Read a weather forecast
steps: '40% chance of rain' means a 40% chance of measurable rain at a given point in the area.
Wind chill and heat index describe how it feels on skin.
Watches mean conditions are possible; warnings mean it's happening or imminent.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Where your water comes from
steps: The water cycle: evaporation, condensation into clouds, precipitation, runoff and groundwater.
Most fresh water is locked in ice or underground.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: The printing press changed everything
steps: Gutenberg's movable-type press (~1440) made books far cheaper.
Literacy and the spread of ideas accelerated, fueling the Reformation and the Scientific Revolution.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Why the Roman Empire split
steps: By the late 200s it was too large to govern from one place.
It was divided into Western and Eastern halves.
The West fell in 476; the East (Byzantine Empire) lasted until 1453.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: The Industrial Revolution
steps: Starting in Britain in the late 1700s, machines and steam power moved work from homes to factories.
Cities grew fast, along with new wealth and harsh working conditions.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: Primary vs secondary sources
steps: Primary sources were created at the time (letters, photos, records).
Secondary sources interpret them later (textbooks, documentaries).
Check who made a source, when, and why.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)

items.title: The Cold War in one card
steps: 1947–1991 rivalry between the US and the Soviet Union.
No direct war between them, but an arms race, a space race, and proxy wars.
It ended with the collapse of the USSR in 1991.
items.sourceName: Lumen explainer card (written summary of well-established facts)
